purpose: Watercolor blooms revealed by collecting lights; alpha preserved in WebP. In-game gilding, paper, variable-pressure trails and print layout are rendered in Canvas.
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: transparent pigment-bloom atlas for an original Japanese ink-and-paper sailing game.
Primary request: FOUR distinct exquisitely delicate circular watercolor blooms, arranged in a precise TWO-column TWO-row grid on a 1024 by 1024 TRANSPARENT canvas, each inside a 512px square cell. Each bloom is centered, no larger than 420px across, separate with ample transparent padding. View flat overhead.
Style/medium: refined Japanese mineral pigment and watery ink on handmade washi; genuine granulation, wet-in-wet blooms, soft capillary edges, pooling rings, intricate white negative-space dendritic veins like frost, tidal deltas or mineral crystals. Small sparse fragments of antique gold leaf caught in the veins, fine and tasteful. Restrained, lyrical, luminous, organic, not photographic, not flat vector, not neon. Low saturation with plenty of translucency: underlying paper should be visible when composited. No solid opaque background anywhere.
Cell 1 top-left: warm honey ochre and pale antique-gold bloom.
Cell 2 top-right: dusty rose, pale copper and soft terracotta bloom.
Cell 3 bottom-left: muted celadon, moss and jade bloom.
Cell 4 bottom-right: slate indigo and misty blue bloom.
Each stain has a broad airy irregular circular silhouette, subtle branching tide-like marks and a small hollow pale center. Not literal flowers, no botanical stems, no island rocks, no boats, no scenery, no objects, no text, no borders, no watermark, no frame, no labels. The canvas outside the four separate watercolor pools must have real alpha transparency. Do not paint a paper background: the game supplies its own paper.
